Forecast Discussion

Two areas of low pressure off the coast pull away to the east-northeast today. A weak cold front crossed from west to east around midday. Early fog yields to a mostly cloudy day, with more clouds west than east. A shower or two is possible in the afternoon, mostly along the western escarpment (near the NC/TN border).

High pressure moves across the Great Lakes Tuesday, and sunshine returns. Tuesday night is mostly clear and colder

By Wednesday, that high is centered in New England and wedges cold air down the east side of the Appalachians. Wednesday is cold, and clouds arrive quickly.

Low pressure moves along the Gulf Coast Wednesday and up the Atlantic Coast on Thanksgiving Day. Rain develops from south to north Wednesday evening. Rain may be heavy at times late Wednesday night into Thanksgiving morning. It tapers off Thursday afternoon, with a few showers possible into the evening.

Much colder air arrives late Thursday night on gusty northwest winds. Flurries or snow showers are possible after midnight, mostly at higher elevations in the west. Friday is cold and windy, and flurries remain possible.

High pressure settles over the Southeast this weekend. Saturday is dry and not as cold by afternoon. Sunday is milder with increasing clouds, and I cannot rule out a stray shower Sunday evening.
